raw_response:
I have been doing this for 25 years on this land. I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is familiar to me. My 3 mu grows wheat first, then I turn it over to maize after harvest — same land, both seasons. That is how everyone around here does it, and it is what my family needs to eat and sell.

**My thinking on wheat:**
I plant in October after the last maize comes off. I always buy improved seed from the agro-supply shop in town — not the fanciest new variety, just whatever reliable one the shop recommends and my neighbors are using. I have been burned before planting something too new. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, then top-dress with urea at jointing. With my well, I irrigate at sowing if the soil is dry, then at jointing and heading — sometimes once more at grain fill if it looks dry. I spray herbicide in early spring and then once for aphids or rust before harvest. I use the rotary tiller after the maize stalks come down to work the residue in. I expect around 420 jin per mu — maybe more if spring rains cooperate.

**My thinking on maize:**
Right after wheat harvest in June I get the maize in fast. I buy hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or something similar, that is what the whole village uses. I do not gamble on unknown varieties. I apply base fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium at planting, then topdress nitrogen at tasseling time when the plant needs it most. I irrigate at tasseling and again if August turns hot and dry — 2 or 3 times with my well. Two pesticide sprays for armyworm and corn borer. I harvest in late September, early October. Around 550 jin per mu most years.

**Why I do it this way:**
Some family members earn money off-farm, so I am not desperate to take risks. I keep inputs moderate — not the absolute minimum, but I do not overspend either. My land is only 3 mu so I manage it all myself with family help. I do not change things much year to year unless something went wrong.
